svg.title: Fixed blocks versus content-defined blocks after inserting bytes at the start
svg.desc: With fixed 4 MiB boundaries, inserting bytes at the start shifts all content, so every block after the insert is new: 6 of 6 blocks upload. With content-defined boundaries, cuts follow the content, so only the first block, which contains the insert, is new: 1 of 5 blocks uploads.
svg.text: insert a few bytes at the very start of a file
every cut lands on shifted content, so every hash changes
content-defined boundaries (cut where the rolling hash hits)
cuts follow the content, so blocks 2 to 5 keep their hashes
